1. (Currently amended) A method for treating an ocular condition, the method comprising: administering to the interior of an eye a composition comprising a therapeutically effective amount of a macromolecular anti-angiogenic component (MAAC) to a mammal suffering from an ocular condition, wherein the composition also comprises a viscosity inducing component in an amount effective to increase the viscosity of the composition to a viscosity at 25°C of at least about 10 cps at a shear rate of about 0.1/second, wherein said viscosity inducing component is injectable into the vitreous of a mammalian eye without permanently diminishing visual acuity.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein said composition comprises a solution.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein said composition comprises a gel.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein said composition comprises a suspension.

5. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein a symptom of the ocular condition is selected from the group consisting of macular degeneration, choroidal neovascularization, retinopathy, and diabetic retinopathy.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 5 wherein the MAAC comprises an agent selected from the group consisting of a nucleic acid (an oligonucleotide) and a protein.

7. (Currently amended) The method of claim 6 wherein said MAAC comprises a nucleic acid.

8. (Currently amended) The method of claim 7 wherein said nucleic acid comprises a therapeutic agent selected from the group consisting of an aptamer, an RNAi, a ribozyme, and an antisense oligonucleotide.

9. (Currently amended) The method of claim 8 wherein said MAAC comprises a therapeutic agent selected from the group consisting of siRNA Z, pegaptanib, and Cand5.

10. (Currently amended) The method of claim 8 wherein said MAAC comprises at least one nucleic acid having a nucleic acid sequence having at least 80% identity to a nucleotide sequence selected from the group consisting of SEQ ID NO:1, SEQ ID NO:2, SEQ ID NO:3, SEQ ID NO:4, SEQ ID NO:5, SEQ ID NO:6, SEQ ID NO:7, SEQ ID NO:8, SEQ ID NO:9, SEQ ID NO:10, SEQ ID NO:11, SEQ ID NO:14, SEQ ID NO:15, SEQ ID NO:22, and SEQ ID NO:23, and nucleotide sequences corresponding to any of these containing at least one modified nucleotide.

11. (Currently amended) The method of claim 10 wherein said nucleic acid has a nucleotide sequence having at least 90% identity to a nucleotide sequence selected from said group.

12. (Currently amended) The method of claim 11 wherein said nucleic acid has a nucleotide sequence having at least 95% identity to a nucleotide sequence selected from said group.

13. (Currently amended) The method of claim 11 wherein said nucleic acid has at least 95% identity to a nucleotide sequence selected from said group.

14. (Currently amended) The method of claim 6 wherein said MAAC comprises a protein.

15. (Currently amended) The method of claim 14 wherein said protein is selected from the group consisting of an antibody and an angiogenesis inhibitor.

20. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein said viscosity inducing component comprises a compound selected from the group consisting of a hyaluronic acid, a cross-linked hyaluronic acid, and a mixture thereof.

21. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein said viscosity inducing component comprises a compound having a molecular weight in the range from about 10,000 Daltons to about 2 million Daltons.

24. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein said viscosity inducing component has a viscosity of at least about 100 cps at a shear rate of 0.1/second at 25°C.

25. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein said viscosity inducing component has a viscosity of at least about 1000 cps at a shear rate of 0.1/second at 25°C.

26. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein said viscosity inducing component has a viscosity of at least about 10,000 cps at a shear rate of 0.1/second at 25°C.

27. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein said viscosity inducing component has a viscosity of at least about 70,000 cps at a shear rate of 0.1/second at 25°C.

28. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein said viscosity inducing component has a viscosity of at least about 200,000 cps at a shear rate of 0.1/second at 25°C.

29. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein said viscosity inducing component has a viscosity of at least about 250,000 cps at a shear rate of 0.1/second at 25°C.

30. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein said viscosity inducing component has a viscosity of at least about 300,000 cps at a shear rate of 0.1/second at 25°C.

31. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein said composition is administered to the interior of said eye by placement into the posterior segment of the eye through a 27-gauge needle.

32. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein said condition comprises a condition of the posterior segment of the eye.

33. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein said condition comprises a condition selected from the group consisting of macular degeneration, retinopathy, and diabetic retinopathy.

34. (Currently amended) A pharmaceutical composition for intravitreal administration to treat an ocular condition comprising a MAAC and a high viscosity hyaluronic acid carrier.
